DNA extraction and PCR amplification methods were performed in the same way as for the microbial community structure tests. Metagenomic sequencing was conducted using the Illumina NovaSeq sequencing platform (Shanghai Meiji Biomedical Technology Co., Ltd., China). Firstly, the optimized sequences were assembled by splicing using the assembler software (MEGAHIT, https://github.com/voutcn/megahit, version 1.1.2) based on the principle of succinct de Bruijn graphs (Li et al. 2015). Among the splicing results, contigs larger than 300 bp were screened as the final assembly results. ORF prediction of contigs from the splicing results was subsequently performed using Prodigal/MetaGene (http://metagene.cb.k.u-tokyo.ac.jp/) (Noguchi et al. 2006). Genes with nucleic acid lengths greater than 100 bp were selected and translated into amino acid sequences. In the construction of non-redundant gene set, the gene sequences predicted from all samples were clustered (parameters: 90% identity, 90% coverage) using CD-HIT (http://www.bioinformatics.org/cd-hit/, version 4.6.1) (Fu et al. 2012), and the longest gene in each class was taken as the representative sequence to construct the non-redundant gene set. 
High-quality reads from each sample were individually compared to the non-redundant gene set (95% identity) using SOAPaligner software (http://soap.genomics.org.cn/, version 2.21) (Li et al. 2008) to statistically characterize the abundance information of genes in the corresponding samples. Diamond (http://www.diamondsearch.org/index.php, version 0.8.35) (Buchfink et al. 2015) was utilized to align amino acid sequences with the NR database (BLASTP with an e-value of 1eˉ5). Simultaneously, employing the taxonomic information database within the NR repository, we acquired species annotations. Ultimately, species abundance was computed by summing the gene abundances corresponding to the respective species. Additionally, Diamond was employed to align amino acid sequences with the KEGG database (BLASTP with an e-value of 1eˉ5), providing the KEGG functions associated with the respective genes. The abundances of functional categories were calculated by summing the abundances of genes corresponding to KO, Pathway, EC, and Module.
